public_rationale: EdSurge reported on May 2, 2024 that LAUSD's generative AI chatbot had reached about 55,000 students at 100 schools in a soft launch [e2]. The chatbot shut down on June 14, 2024; information remained accessible through the platform, and the district planned to restore the chatbot [e3]. The 74 reported that officials acknowledged at the September 10, 2024 bankruptcy hearing that AllHere could not fulfill its LAUSD contract [e4]. Together, the deployment, shutdown and reported inability to fulfill the contract establish one unsuccessful implementation under the contract's definition [e2–e4]. This supports the forecast when the substantial deployment at a public institution counts as enterprise scale [e2].
limitations: The result depends on including public institutions and treating this soft launch as enterprise scale.
The bankruptcy-hearing acknowledgment is reported by The 74; the underlying transcript was not obtained.
Surviving platform features and restart plans limit conclusions about permanent abandonment or loss of all project value.
One unsuccessful implementation establishes neither a general failure rate nor that model limitations caused the failure.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Not every enterprise-scale generative AI project will succeed.

statement.excerpt: And of course not every enterprise-scale experiment will be successful.
statement.document_title: The Rise and Fall of ChatGPT?

our_interpretation: The surrounding discussion identifies the experiments as generative AI projects.
The ordinary reading requires at least one unsuccessful project, without predicting a failure rate.
Enterprise scale means substantial operational deployment across a large organization. This includes public institutions.
An implementation that shuts down and cannot fulfill its contracted purpose counts as unsuccessful, even if some infrastructure remains useful.
criteria.support_condition: After publication, at least one substantially deployed organizational generative AI project is discontinued unsuccessfully or demonstrably fails its intended implementation.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Every project within the claim's scope succeeds. With no deadline or closed population, a finite collection of successes cannot establish this.

evidence.explanation: The district announced an operational launch following pilot testing. Deployment was not yet districtwide; company_disclosure is the schema's closest category for an institution's own announcement.

The report identifies the generative technology and says the soft launch covered about 55,000 students at 100 schools. That supports substantial organizational deployment, while leaving room to dispute whether a soft launch meets Marcus's unstated scale threshold.

evidence.locator: Paragraph following discussion of the surviving online platform
evidence.explanation: The report dates the chatbot shutdown to June 14 but records plans to restore it and continued access to underlying information. This limits any claim that all project assets became worthless or that the initial shutdown alone established permanent abandonment.

evidence.locator: Paragraph beginning Instead, court records show
evidence.explanation: Reporting from Tuesday's bankruptcy hearing documents inability to fulfill the district contract and preparations to close the supplier. Together with the deployed chatbot's shutdown, this establishes failure of the original implementation, beyond a routine temporary interruption.

conclusive_event.meets_rule: The 74's account of the hearing documents inability to fulfill the LAUSD contract. Combined with the substantial generative AI deployment [e2] and subsequent shutdown [e3], this establishes one unsuccessful enterprise-scale implementation after August 24, 2023, meeting the early-resolution rule.
